arxiv-2008-13674.title: Magmatic channelisation by reactive and shear-driven instabilities at mid-ocean ridges: a combined analysis
arxiv-2008-13674.creator: D. W. Rees Jones 1,2,, H. Zhang 2,3 and R. F. Katz 2 1 University of St Andrews, School of Mathematics and Statistics, Mathematical Institute, North Haugh, St Andrews, KY16 9SS, United Kingdom. 2 University of Oxford, Department of Earth Sciences, South Parks Road, Oxford, OX1 3AN, United Kingdom. 3
arxiv-2008-13674.description: Abstract {summary} It is generally accepted that melt extraction from the mantle at mid-ocean ridges is concentrated in narrow regions of elevated melt fraction called channels. Two feedback mechanisms have been proposed to explain why these channels grow by linear instability: shear flow of partially molten mantle and reactive flow of the ascending magma.

arxiv-2205-15640.title: Exact solution Ising-like 2 × 2 × ∞ 2\times 2\times\infty models with multispin interactions
arxiv-2205-15640.creator: Pavel Khrapov, Veronika Nikishina
arxiv-2205-15640.description: Abstract . The paper considers the generalized Ising model in the 2 × 2 × ∞ 2\times 2\times\infty strip with a Hamiltonian invariant with respect to the central axis of rotation through the angle π / 2 \pi/2 , which includes all possible multiplicative interactions of an even number of spins in the unit cube.

arxiv-2301-04786.title: Distinct topological configurations of equatorial timelike circular orbit for spherically symmetric (hairy) black holes
arxiv-2301-04786.creator: Xu Ye, Shao-Wen Wei
arxiv-2301-04786.description: Abstract Topology is a promising approach toward to the light ring in a generic black hole background, and equatorial timelike circular orbit in a stationary black hole background. In this paper, we consider the distinct topological configurations of the timelike circular orbits in static, spherically symmetric, and asymptotic flat black holes.

arxiv-2303-10947.title: Flow fluctuations and kinetic freeze-out of identified hadrons at energies available at the CERN Super Proton Synchrotron
arxiv-2303-10947.creator: Sudhir Pandurang Rode, Partha Pratim Bhaduri, Amaresh Jaiswal
arxiv-2303-10947.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Sudhir Pandurang Rode, Partha Pratim Bhaduri, Amaresh Jaiswal. We investigate the effect of flow fluctuations, incorporated in non boost-invariant blast-wave model, on kinetic freeze-out parameters of identified hadrons in low energy relativistic heavy-ion collisions. For the purpose of this study, we use the transverse momentum spectra of the identified hadrons produced in central Pb–Pb collisions, at SPS energies ranging from E Lab = 20 ​ A − 158 ​ A \rm E_{Lab}=20A-158A GeV, and analyze them within a modified non boost-invariant blast wave model.

arxiv-2306-00929.title: Large Charge ’t Hooft Limit of 𝒩 = 4 \mathcal{N}=4 Super-Yang-Mills
arxiv-2306-00929.description: Abstract The planar integrability of 𝒩 = 4 \mathcal{N}=4 super-Yang-Mills (SYM) is the cornerstone for numerous exact observables. We show that the large charge sector of the SU ⁡ ( 2 ) {\rm SU}(2) 𝒩 = 4 \mathcal{N}=4 SYM provides another interesting solvable corner which exhibits striking similarities despite being far from the planar limit.

arxiv-2310-01062.title: Bayesian inference methodology to characterize the dust emissivity at far-infrared and submillimeter frequencies 2024 Bayesian inference methodology to characterize the dust emissivity at far-infrared and submillimeter frequencies – B
arxiv-2310-01062.creator: Debabrata Adak, Shabbir Shaikh, Srijita Sinha, Tuhin Ghosh, Francois Boulanger, Guilaine Lagache, Tarun Souradeep, Marc-Antoine Miville-Deschênes
arxiv-2310-01062.description: Abstract We present a Bayesian inference method to characterise the dust emission properties using the well-known dust- Hi \mathsc{Hi} correlation in the diffuse interstellar medium at Planck frequencies ν ≥ 217 \nu\geq 217 GHz. We use the Galactic Hi \mathsc{Hi} map from the Galactic All-Sky Survey (GASS) as a template to trace the Galactic dust emission.

arxiv-2410-09726.title: Modeling glasses from first principles using random structure sampling
arxiv-2410-09726.creator: Laszlo Wolf, Andrew Novick, Vladan Stevanović ∗
arxiv-2410-09726.description: Abstract We present an approach to approximating static properties of glasses without experimental inputs rooted in the first-principles random structure sampling. In our approach, the glassy system is represented by a collection (composite) of periodic, small-cell (few 10s of atoms) local minima on the potential energy surface.

arxiv-2502-09212.title: LP-LM: No Hallucinations in Question Answering with Logic Programming
arxiv-2502-09212.creator: Katherine Wu, Yanhong A. Liu
arxiv-2502-09212.description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) are able to generate human-like responses to user queries. However, LLMs exhibit inherent limitations, especially because they hallucinate. This paper introduces LP-LM, a system that grounds answers to questions in known facts contained in a knowledge base (KB), facilitated through semantic parsing in Prolog, and always produces answers that are reliable.

arxiv-2503-22276.title: Machine Learning Models for Soil Parameter Prediction Based on Satellite, Weather, Clay and Yield Data
arxiv-2503-22276.creator: Calvin Kammerlander, Viola Kolb, Marinus Luegmair, Lou Scheermann, Maximilian Schmailzl, Marco Seufert, Jiayun Zhang, Denis Dalić, Torsten Schön orcid: 0000-0001-9022-8428
arxiv-2503-22276.description: Abstract Efficient nutrient management and precise fertilization are essential for advancing modern agriculture, particularly in regions striving to optimize crop yields sustainably. The AgroLens project endeavors to address this challenge by developing Machine Learning (ML)-based methodologies to predict soil nutrient levels without reliance on laboratory tests.

arxiv-2508-03209.title: GeoShield: Safeguarding Geolocation Privacy from Vision-Language Models via Adversarial Perturbations
arxiv-2508-03209.creator: Xinwei Liu, Xiaojun Jia, Simeng Qin, Yuan Xun, Xiaochun Cao
arxiv-2508-03209.description: Abstract Vision-Language Models (VLMs) such as GPT-4o now demonstrate a remarkable ability to infer users’ locations from public shared images, posing a substantial risk to geoprivacy. Although adversarial perturbations offer a potential defense, current methods are ill-suited for this scenario: they often perform poorly on high-resolution images and low perturbation budgets, and may introduce irrelevant semantic content.

arxiv-2510-21691.title: On Uncertainty Calibration for Equivariant Functions
arxiv-2510-21691.creator: Edward Berman berman.ed@northeastern.edu, Jacob Ginesin ginesin@cmu.edu, Marco Pacini mpacini@fbk.eu, Robin Walters r.walters@northeastern.edu
arxiv-2510-21691.description: Abstract Data-sparse settings such as robotic manipulation, molecular physics, and galaxy morphology classification are some of the hardest domains for deep learning. For these problems, equivariant networks can help improve modeling across undersampled parts of the input space, and uncertainty estimation can guard against overconfidence.

arxiv-2512-07165.title: MuSASplat: Efficient Sparse-View 3D Gaussian Splats via Lightweight Multi-Scale Adaptation
arxiv-2512-07165.creator: Muyu Xu, Fangneng Zhan, Xiaoqin Zhang, Ling Shao, Shijian Lu
arxiv-2512-07165.description: Abstract Sparse-view 3D Gaussian splatting seeks to render high-quality novel views of 3D scenes from a limited set of input images. While recent pose-free feed-forward methods leveraging pre-trained 3D priors have achieved impressive results, most of them rely on full fine-tuning of large Vision Transformer (ViT) backbones and incur substantial GPU costs.

pmc-12808218.title: Gender dynamics and remittances in the adoption of sustainable agricultural practices in Nepal
pmc-12808218.creator: Giri Prasad Kandel, Mustapha Yakubu Madaki, Tereza Pilarova, Ayat Ullah, Prajal Pradhan, Ioannis Manikas, Miroslava Bavorova
pmc-12808218.description: Agricultural systems in rural Nepal face significant transformation due to climate change and shifting household labour dynamics. Male out-migration, a key but underexplored driver of this change, disrupts traditional gendered labor divisions and reshapes agricultural decision-making. In smallholder farms, traditionally, men are more responsible for tasks like ploughing and harvesting, whereas women take on planting, weeding, and winnowing roles.

pmc-13392240.title: Adsorption based on excitation
pmc-13392240.creator: Shi-Chao Qi, Yan-Yan Han, Yong-Lan Liu, Yun-Jie Zhao, Qi-Qi Huang, Xiao-Qin Liu, Lin-Bing Sun
pmc-13392240.description: Traditionally, adsorption is believed to take place only in the ground state, but here we report an excitation-driven adsorption mode. Composites of metallophthalocyanines and carbonaceous substrates are prepared, among which the potassium-phthalocyanine (KPc)/reduced graphene oxide (RG) composite shows the most typical behavior.

pmc-13632339.title: Mapping the landscape of allele-specific expression in porcine genomes
pmc-13632339.creator: Wen-ye Yao, Marta Gòdia, Lingzhao Fang, Martien A. M. Groenen, Lijing Bai, Kui Li, Ole Madsen
pmc-13632339.description: BackgroundAllele-specific expression (ASE) is the imbalanced expression of two alleles of the same locus. It is quite pervasive among many species and is associated with health and economically relevant traits. ASE is often used to support the identification of variants related to gene expression (cis-eQTL).
